sources.title: Bulgaria's Biennial Transparency Report 2024 under the Paris Agreement
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate and hydrology across source-stated historical periods; future climate-health vulnerabilities; adaptation institutions through 2024.
sources.methodology: Government BTR compiles national climate, hydrological and sector evidence.
sources.limitations: Periods vary; future projections are uncertain.

sources.title: Overlooked: Examining the Impact of Disasters and Climate Shocks on Poverty in the Europe and Central Asia Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Bulgaria case study of the June 2014 flood, published in a 2021 regional report.
sources.methodology: World Bank regional poverty and disaster report; Bulgaria's case box synthesizes cited event sources.
sources.limitations: The Bulgaria box cites secondary references and does not reproduce an underlying local assessment.

sources.title: Disasters, Accidents, Incidents and Crises in 2024: Final Data
sources.temporal_coverage: Final event and expenditure statistics for 2024, with selected comparisons to 2023.
sources.methodology: Official NSI release presenting final annual counts of crisis events, declared disasters, geographic coverage and public expenditure.
sources.limitations: Categories include non-climate crises and accidents; the release does not attribute events to climate change or disaggregate household impacts.

sources.title: The Water Crises of Bulgaria: Analysis and Solutions (Summary)
sources.temporal_coverage: Climate observations include 1991–2020; water-sector indicators are reported as current in the March 2026 summary; irrigation figures include 2024.
sources.methodology: MOEW minister/deputy-minister report summary drawing on climate observations and water-sector/operator statistics.
sources.limitations: Summary-level government analysis; figures use varied periods and some operator records are not externally verifiable.

sources.title: Country Report Bulgaria 2026 (Staff Working Document and Annexes)
sources.organization: European Commission, Directorate-General for Economic and Financial Affairs
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 country analysis; mixed indicators from 2013–2025 and adaptation programming for 2021–2027.
sources.methodology: European Commission country staff working document synthesizing Bulgarian and EU indicators, policy documents and implementation evidence; Annex 10 addresses adaptation and preparedness.
sources.limitations: Indicators use different reference periods; reported plans and coverage are not household-level outcome measurements.

claims.paraphrase: 1981–2010 drought mapping identifies the Danube corridor and central north to the Pre-Balkans; Northeast Bulgaria/Dobrudzha is most affected, with pockets around Blagoevgrad, Petrich–Sandanski and Mesta valley.
geographies: central northern Bulgaria to the Pre-Balkans

claims.paraphrase: Struma valley near Kresna Gorge is hottest: some years had 6–8 days above 40°C; 1961–2020 records show 40–55 hot days/year there versus 2–3 on the northern Black Sea coast.
geographies: Struma River valley near Kresna Gorge
claims.limitations: Historical regional averages, not household exposure.

claims.paraphrase: BTR expects climate-related heat/extreme-weather morbidity and mortality to rise, disproportionately affecting children, older people, people with chronic illness and low-income groups.
claims.scenario: No emissions scenario or period is specified; medium-term is a working horizon.
claims.limitations: BTR notes data and health-model uncertainty.

claims.locator: PDF p. 143, projections of annual precipitation
claims.paraphrase: BTR projects lower precipitation in southern and southeastern Bulgaria under SSP5-8.5 in the far future, potentially compounding hotter conditions.
claims.scenario: SSP5-8.5, far future as labeled in the report.

claims.paraphrase: For the June 2014 torrential-rain flash flood in Asparuhovo (Varna), the WB box reports 122 evacuated families, Roma ownership of 60% of destroyed houses, and 14 deaths, most among Roma.
claims.limitations: Single historical case; WB-reported casualty count was not reconciled with other reports.

claims.paraphrase: The report links unequal flood losses in Asparuhovo to informal Roma housing that failed building-code/zoning standards and to inadequate municipal prevention; it says no clear data show how many Roma live in flood-prone areas.
claims.limitations: Regional synthesis relies on cited secondary references.

claims.paraphrase: NSI records 38 2024 disaster declarations, mainly for wildfires, floods, drought and hail; declarations for drinking-water shortage due to drought increased from 2023.
affected_groups: residents of municipalities under disaster declaration
claims.limitations: NSI gives no climate attribution; categories are mixed-hazard.

claims.paraphrase: 2024 declared disasters partly or fully affected 47 municipalities in 19 administrative regions; those municipalities had 1,308,715 residents, 20.3% of Bulgaria's population.
geographies: 47 municipalities across 19 administrative regions; names not enumerated in the release text
affected_groups: residents of municipalities partly or fully under disaster declaration
claims.limitations: Resident totals are not counts of directly harmed people.

claims.paraphrase: MOEW reports 60.25% overall water losses; named-town loss rates are highest in Shumen (83.67%), Pernik (83.25%), Targovishte (73.61%), Haskovo (72.41%), Yambol (70.60%) and Pazardzhik (67.69%).
claims.limitations: Service-loss indicators are not attributed to climate change.

claims.locator: PDF p. 15, section 5.3, Small settlements are the most vulnerable
claims.paraphrase: MOEW says small and peripheral settlements are particularly vulnerable to restrictions, low pressure and interruptions; only 1,869 of 5,302 meter zones have continuous flow/pressure measurement with data archiving.
geographies: small and peripheral settlements across Bulgaria
affected_groups: residents of small and peripheral settlements
claims.limitations: Report identifies limited measurement and information as system gaps.

claims.locator: PDF p. 4, section 6.4, irrigation capacity in 2024
claims.paraphrase: In 2024, Irrigation Systems supplied 342,614 decares against 5.376 million decares of design capacity (about 6.4%); MOEW says long-term decline limits agricultural production and increases drought vulnerability.
claims.limitations: Company-served irrigation area is not total farm irrigation.

claims.locator: PDF p. 3, summary; pp. 23–24, sections 8 and 11
claims.paraphrase: MOEW says climate change amplifies, but does not fully explain, water stress; underinvestment, fragmented responsibility, weak expertise and data gaps also contribute. It recommends monitoring, modernization, river/flood planning and local water retention.
claims.limitations: Recommendations describe proposed actions, not completed outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 96–97, Annex 10, adaptation governance and subnational implementation
claims.paraphrase: The Commission says adaptation barriers include implementation capacity, data availability and cross-level coordination; the national risk assessment is outdated and comparable regional/local risk information is lacking for prioritization.
claims.limitations: Commission assessment, not local household-level data.

claims.locator: PDF p. 97, Annex 10, Environment Operational Programme and implementation
claims.paraphrase: The 2021–2027 Environment Operational Programme provides EUR 225.64 million in climate-adaptation support; the Commission says planning-to-investment links and use of climate, hydrological and early-warning information need strengthening.
claims.limitations: Programme allocation is not evidence of spending or outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF p. 97, Annex 10, Covenant of Mayors and local planning indicators
claims.paraphrase: Only around 24% of Bulgaria's population lives in Covenant of Mayors coverage; 10 of 49 cities made adaptation commitments and 44% of signatories submitted SECAPs on time. Sofia has an adaptation strategy; Burgas a development vision.
claims.limitations: Commitments and timely reporting do not demonstrate effectiveness.

search_audit.query: Bulgaria climate vulnerability subnational flood drought heat Roma vulnerable groups primary
search_audit.outcome: Opened government climate-risk passages, current water-system evidence, 2024 official disaster data and the Asparuhovo Roma case; no harmonized municipal household exposure dataset was found.

search_audit.query: Bulgaria climate change drought conflict social tensions violence security official report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source stated a climate-to-armed, intercommunal or political-violence pathway. The Roma flood case documents unequal disaster impacts, not conflict propensity or a climate-FCV link.

search_audit.query: Bulgaria conflict violence climate adaptation disaster risk local capacity climate official report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source identified conflict or violence disrupting climate adaptation or disaster response in Bulgaria; the search found current capacity and governance constraints without an FCV mechanism.

search_audit.query: site:government.bg Bulgaria national climate adaptation strategy municipalities capacity flood drought PDF
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed the BTR's strategy/planning account, MOEW water-management recommendations and the Commission's current implementation and municipal-capacity assessment; plans are distinguished from achieved outcomes.

gaps: No inspected public source established a climate-related armed/intercommunal violence pathway or an FCV-to-adaptation pathway; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.
The 2024 NSI release gives population totals for municipalities partly or fully affected by disaster declarations, not direct counts of people harmed, and its text does not name those municipalities.
The Asparuhovo Roma evidence is a regional World Bank synthesis of cited sources; its casualty count was not independently reconciled with other event reports.

The Commission finds the national climate-risk assessment outdated and current comparable regional/local risk information insufficient; no inspected source supplied household-level vulnerability data for smaller settlements.
